text:
The pedestrian’s statement is inadmissible hearsay if offered to prove the man switched lanes without signaling, because it is an out-of-court assertion of fault and no hearsay exception clearly applies. The note’s claim that every hearsay exception requires an identified, cross-examinable declarant is incorrect—excited utterances and present sense impressions, for example, can be admitted even if the declarant is unidentified and unavailable.  
CONFIDENCE: 90
